meta.purpose: Single source of truth for every failure mode this platform has discovered. Each record names the framework component that must catch it and the verdict it must emit; tests/validation/test_failure_benchmarks.py replays the whole ledger and scripts/add_failure_benchmark.py refuses to register a mode no component actually catches.
flywheel: discover a failure mode (audit / red team / live)
register it: detector + expected_verdict + input (add_failure_benchmark.py RUNS the detector and refuses if it does not fire)
the meta-test replays the whole ledger forever (regression against catastrophic forgetting)
a documented mode no detector catches goes to known_gaps until the framework is extended

benchmarks.title: GBM top-N boundary decided by identical model scores
benchmarks.failure_mode: The shipped top-10 selection is decided by sort-tie order, not by signal, so the list flips arbitrarily when the universe or data snapshot changes.
benchmarks.symptom: Shipped gbm_picks carry byte-identical scores; adding one row / 21 names produced a 2/10 overlap (MISMATCH) on the same month.
benchmarks.evidence: reports/gbm_picks/2026-09.json + reports/gbm_picks/2026-10.json (2026-10 top-10 has only 5 unique scores; boundary score shared by 3 names). boundary_stability returns has_exact_ties=True; the audit maps this to AMBER and deployment_gate blocks it.

benchmarks.title: GBM mean IC flips sign across years
benchmarks.failure_mode: A single point estimate hides that the strategy's per-period IC is not sign-consistent through time.
benchmarks.symptom: Yearly mean IC changes sign 3 times in 7 years; the same strategy re-run from a later window start flipped mean IC from +0.0082 to -0.0076.

benchmarks.title: S&P500 GBM Sharpe flips sign with the test window
benchmarks.failure_mode: The headline window is the only window; the sign of the metric is a function of where the test window starts.
benchmarks.symptom: Sharpe +0.362 full window but -0.026 since 2024 (and -0.0038 mean IC) on the same configuration.

benchmarks.title: Reported Sharpe is an order of magnitude above the IC-implied IR
benchmarks.failure_mode: Two numbers that cannot both be true sit in the same report because they are never cross-checked.
benchmarks.symptom: Sharpe 0.963 next to mean monthly IC 0.0082 over 71 months: IC*sqrt(breadth) implies an IR ~0.07, not ~0.96.

benchmarks.title: S&P500 expansion result carried by a single year (the distressed-stock lottery)
benchmarks.failure_mode: One observation (year) is more than half of all gross positive return: the strategy is that observation.
benchmarks.symptom: 2021 contributes 60% of gross positive annual mean IC (top-2 = 93%); removing it erases the effect.
benchmarks.evidence: reports/xsec_gbm_sp500.json:monthly_ic.by_year (7 annual means; top1_share=0.603, top2_share=0.925). Flagged SINGLE_EVENT_DRIVEN by scripts/validate_reports.py.

benchmarks.title: weekend_gap long leg needs its best 2 trades
benchmarks.failure_mode: The conclusion is the arithmetic of a handful of observations: remove the best k<=2 trades and significance is gone.
benchmarks.symptom: Removing the 2 best of 13 long-only trades moves the two-sided p from 0.026 to ~0.11; 2 trades carry 63% of gross profit.

benchmarks.title: weekend_gap red-team series is destroyed by ONE observation
benchmarks.failure_mode: A more marginal baseline makes the fragility worse: a single best observation is the whole conclusion.
benchmarks.symptom: The red team's published 13-event return series has baseline t=2.146; removing its single best event kills significance (k=1).

benchmarks.title: meta-labeling is indistinguishable from zero (honest negative result)
benchmarks.failure_mode: An event-level mean that cannot be distinguished from zero is reported as a result rather than as NOISE.
benchmarks.symptom: LOO AUC ~0.5; 50 event net returns give t=1.14, win rate Wilson interval straddles 0.5.

benchmarks.title: Funding-rate signal has no edge over buy-and-hold
benchmarks.failure_mode: A positive-looking mean is inside the noise band; every variant underperforms the benchmark.
benchmarks.symptom: Best funding variant Sharpe 0.30 vs basket buy-and-hold 0.447; event-level t=1.17 -> indistinguishable from zero.

benchmarks.title: On-chain BTC signal Sharpe is not sign-consistent across years
benchmarks.failure_mode: 8 years with 5 negative Sharpe years: the strategy's sign is decided by the year.
benchmarks.symptom: Yearly strategy Sharpe is negative 5/8 years; total -71.6% vs BTC buy-and-hold +623%.

benchmarks.title: overnight_gap daily-frequency leg dies after 2023
benchmarks.failure_mode: The generalization of an event strategy loses its sign in the most recent regime while the pooled number stays positive.
benchmarks.symptom: Per-year PnL for the market-close / 2% leg is negative in 6 of 8 years; sign consistency 0.75.

benchmarks.title: FOMC decision-day effect is a 2020-22 ZIRP artifact
benchmarks.failure_mode: A calendar effect pooled across eras hides that it only exists in the zero-rate regime.
benchmarks.symptom: Basket T-day mean return is -0.02% (2016-19), +3.41% (2020-22), -0.22% (2023-26): the sign is era-dependent.

benchmarks.title: Same month re-run gives a 2/10 overlap with the shipped picks
benchmarks.failure_mode: A conclusion that cannot be reproduced under another snapshot / execution path is not a conclusion.
benchmarks.symptom: run_monthly_gbm.py --as-of 2021-06 reproduced only 2 of the 10 stored picks (score ties + universe drift).
benchmarks.evidence: Constructed from the documented 2026-09 crisis (run_monthly_gbm.py --as-of 2021-06 -> 2/10 MISMATCH). The stored picks are the *symptom* (exact ties); the two selections here represent the rerun vs the archive.

known_gaps.title: FTX single-event LOSS dominance is not caught
known_gaps.failure_mode: A strategy's realised P&L is dominated by one catastrophic event (the 2022-11-11 FTX collapse, -21.1%).
known_gaps.why_open: SINGLE_EVENT_DRIVEN is defined on *gross positive* return (top1_share over winners only), and leave_k_worst_out only fires when removing large losses FLIPS the sign. A single large loss inside an otherwise positive series is invisible to both. The funding report's own findings name FTX as the 2022 P&L driver (reports/funding_rolling_backtest.json q6/answer), yet no framework component turns that into a verdict.
known_gaps.would_need: A loss-side concentration check (e.g. SINGLE_LOSS_DRIVEN on gross negative return, or a leave-k-worst-out that flags a single loss > 50% of gross loss).

known_gaps.title: Boundary churn under a universe/row change is not auto-detected
known_gaps.failure_mode: Adding one row (BAYRY) or 21 names flips an entire month's top-10 (2/10 overlap), but the stored artefacts only let the detector see exact ties, not the churn.
known_gaps.why_open: boundary_stability on the stored picks returns verdict STABLE (mean flip rate 0.0) because the tied block does not straddle the top-N cut in the two stored months; it surfaces has_exact_ties=True (AMBER) but not ARBITRARY. The ++21-stock universe variant that produced the MISMATCH was never persisted as a second score snapshot, so the churn itself cannot be recomputed from the ledger.
known_gaps.would_need: Persist the perturbed-universe score snapshot alongside the shipped picks, then boundary_stability (or reproducibility_probe) can compare the two selections directly.
known_gaps.evidence: reports/gbm_picks/ (2 stored months; verdict STABLE / has_exact_ties True)
